quotes.file: Tengyur/04 DBU MA_Middle Way School (Madhyamaka)/VOL 1 (TZA)/TD03824_DBU MA RTZA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA SHES RAB CES BYA BA (Prajñā Nāma Mūla Madhyamaka Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: དབུ་མ་རྩ་བའི་ཚིག་ལེའུར་བྱས་པ་ཤེས་རབ། I.1 — the treatise's first verse, immediately after the eight-negation homage
quotes.why: Nāgārjuna's own words, in the root text rather than in any of the three commentaries that quote them here. This is the verse the paragraph cites.

Chökyi Gyaltsen's own Madhyamaka textbook opens the same topic with a division this paragraph does not make: consequences first, probative reasons second. What p80 calls the whole is there only the second half.

quotes.citation: དབུ་མའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the same enumeration, one level down
quotes.why: The same author's list of the five probative reasons, word for word as in this paragraph, showing that p80 is transplanting a settled Madhyamaka schema rather than devising one.

quotes.citation: དབུ་མའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — why the vajra-sliver is taken second
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's reason for the ordering: Nāgārjuna and Āryadeva themselves establish emptiness principally by the vajra-sliver, which is why this paragraph takes it up before the other three.

quotes.citation: དབུ་མའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — on what the root verse does and does not do
quotes.why: The same author says the verse states only the thesis and does not set out a valid probative reason — which is not obviously what this paragraph does with it. This is the sharpest tension in the passage.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། — near the opening, on how ground, path and aspects are known to be unproduced
quotes.why: Haribhadra's own words are where this excursus attaches: the reasonings are named here as 'free from being one or many, and so forth'. The paragraph is unpacking his 'and so forth'.

quotes.text: སོགས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཟེགས་མར། རང་ལས་མ་ཡིན་གཞན་ལས་མིན། ། གཉི་ག་ལས་མིན་རྒྱུ་མེད་མིན། ། དངོས་པོ་གང་དང་གང་ལ་ཡང་། ། སྐྱེ་བ་ནམ་ཡང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། ། ཞེས་བྱ་བ་དང་།
quotes.why: Dharmamitra unpacks Haribhadra's 'and so forth' as the vajra-sliver — quoting the very verse this paragraph quotes — then dependent origination and the four-alternative refutation. The Indian precedent for the paragraph's list.
Gyaltsab poses exactly the question this excursus answers and gives the same two reasons, adding the curricular point that this establishment happens first at the path of accumulation.

quotes.citation: ལུང་རིགས་ཀྱི་རོལ་མཚོ། — the same schema, with three members
quotes.why: Ngok Lotsāwa, four centuries earlier and outside this curriculum, has the same classification by what each reason examines — but stops at three. The list this paragraph gives has grown.

quotes.text: དེ་ལྟར་ཡང་དབུ་མའི་རྩ་བ་ལས། བདག་ལས་མ་ཡིན་གཞན་ལས་མིན། ། གཉིས་ལས་མ་ཡིན་རྒྱུ་མེད་མིན། ། དངོས་པོ་གང་དག་གང་ན་ཡང་། ། སྐྱེ་བ་ནམ་ཡང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། ཞེས་སོ། །
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa reaches the same verse inside the Ornament commentary itself, and reaches it the way this paragraph does: as the scriptural seal on a refutation already argued out alternative by alternative.
